skill.name: analyzing-financial-statements
skill.description: Calculates and interprets financial ratios from income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, and market data.
skill.summary: Analyze company financial statements with ratio calculations, benchmark context, and trend interpretation.
skill.author: anthropics

content.value_statement: Financial statement review requires accurate ratio calculations and clear interpretation. This skill calculates ratios, benchmarks results, and explains liquidity, leverage, profitability, efficiency, and valuation signals.
actual_capabilities: Calculates profitability ratios, including ROE, ROA, gross margin, operating margin, and net margin.
Calculates liquidity ratios, including current ratio, quick ratio, and cash ratio.
Calculates leverage, efficiency, valuation, and per-share metrics from structured financial data.
Adds basic interpretations for current ratio, debt-to-equity, ROE, and P/E ratio.
Compares selected ratios against simplified industry benchmarks.
Analyzes multi-period trends when historical ratio data is provided.
limitations: Requires accurate financial statement and market data.
Uses simplified benchmarks and may not match a specific company's peer group.
Does not verify source filings or detect accounting errors.
Does not provide personalized investment, tax, or legal advice.

use_cases.title: Review Company Fundamentals
use_cases.description: Calculate core ratios and summarize financial strengths and weaknesses before deeper analyst review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Classroom Ratio Analysis
use_cases.description: Turn financial statement figures into explained ratios for assignments, case studies, and discussion notes.

use_cases.title: Screen Portfolio Holdings
use_cases.description: Compare liquidity, leverage, profitability, and valuation signals across companies using consistent formulas.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Core Ratios
prompt_templates.prompt: Calculate the main profitability and liquidity ratios from these financial statements. Explain each result in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Financial Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this company's current ratio, quick ratio, debt-to-equity, ROE, and P/E ratio. Identify the strongest and weakest signals.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Industry Benchmarks
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these ratios with the manufacturing benchmarks. Explain whether each metric is poor, acceptable, good, or excellent.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Multi-Year Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these three years of ratio data to assess trend direction, overall financial health, and the top five follow-up questions for management.

output_examples.input: Balance sheet shows current assets of $800,000, inventory of $250,000, and current liabilities of $400,000.
output_examples.output: Current ratio is 2.00, and quick ratio is 1.38. Liquidity appears adequate, but inventory dependence should be reviewed.

output_examples.input: Share price is $50, net income is $150,000, and shares outstanding are 100,000.
output_examples.output: Earnings per share is $1.50, and P/E ratio is 33.33. The valuation appears elevated without supporting growth context.

output_examples.input: ROE moved from 10% to 14% to 18% across three years.
output_examples.output: ROE shows an improving trend. Review whether higher returns came from operational gains, leverage, or one-time items.

best_practices: Provide complete income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, and market data for the same period.
State the industry and time period before asking for benchmark comparisons.
Review unusual ratios against footnotes, one-time events, and accounting policy changes.
anti_patterns: Do not compare ratios across companies without considering industry, scale, and accounting differences.
Do not treat benchmark labels as investment recommendations.
Do not rely on incomplete data without noting missing line items.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It works best with income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, and market data.

faq.question: Can it analyze multiple years?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide historical ratio values and period labels to generate trend direction and percentage changes.

faq.question: Does it replace a financial analyst?
faq.answer: No. It supports calculations and interpretation, but expert judgment is still needed.

faq.question: Which ratios are supported?
faq.answer: It supports profitability, liquidity, leverage, efficiency, valuation, and per-share metrics.

faq.question: Does it provide investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides analytical context and should not be treated as personalized investment advice.

faq.question: Can it use industry benchmarks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes simplified benchmarks for technology, retail, financial, manufacturing, healthcare, and general contexts.
